papers.title: Leveraging serum CHI3L1 and machine learning for non-invasive liver fibrosis diagnostics.
papers.abstract: This study was aimed to develop non-invasive liver fibrosis diagnostic model using chitinase 3-like protein 1 (CHI3L1) based on machine learning (ML).1,011 follow-up patients (556 training/455 validation) were enrolled, staging fibrosis via transient elastography (F01, F2, F23, F34, and F4). Demographic, clinical, and laboratory parameters were collected. Fibrosis-related indicators were selected by differential analysis and correlation analysis. ML models were developed, optimized, and validated. Of 23 initial laboratory indicators, 15 indicators were selected to developed a 5-stage liver fib
papers.summary: This study developed machine learning models that use serum CHI3L1 along with routine clinical and laboratory indicators to non-invasively stage liver fibrosis in 1,011 follow-up patients, validated against transient elastography. The models achieved good discrimination across five fibrosis stages, suggesting CHI3L1-based ML could reduce the need for invasive or imaging-based fibrosis assessment.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Culture-Confirmed Neonatal Sepsis in a Tertiary Neonatal Intensive Care Unit: Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Neonatal sepsis remains a major cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Early diagnosis is challenging because of nonspecific clinical manifestations and delays in laboratory confirmation. Machine learning (ML) approaches using structured electronic health record (EHR) data may improve early risk stratification in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs).
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort study developed machine learning models to predict culture-confirmed neonatal sepsis using structured electronic health record data from a tertiary NICU in a low- and middle-income country setting. The goal was to improve early risk stratification, since neonatal sepsis is a major cause of morbidity and mortality and is difficult to diagnose early due to nonspecific symptoms and delayed lab confirmation.

papers.title: Genomic language model for predicting enhancers and their allele-specific activity in the human genome.
papers.abstract: Predicting and deciphering the regulatory logic of enhancers remains a significant challenge due to their complex sequence features and the absence of consistent genetic or epigenetic signatures that distinguish them from other genomic regions. Existing machine learning methods capture nucleotide composition but often fail to model sequence context effectively.
papers.summary: This paper introduces a genomic language model designed to predict enhancer regions and their allele-specific activity directly from human genome sequence. By leveraging sequence context modeling, it aims to overcome the limitations of prior machine learning methods that rely mainly on nucleotide composition and struggle to capture broader regulatory logic. The approach offers a new way to identify enhancers and interpret how genetic variants affect their activity.

papers.title: De novo Genes in Plants: Origins, Mechanisms, and Functional Implications.
papers.abstract: De novo genes originate from previously non-coding genomic regions. They provide an important source of lineage-specific innovation. In plants, these genes may contribute to adaptation, trait diversity and crop evolution. This review summarizes recent progress in plant de novo gene research. It first discusses major routes of gene birth, including transcription-first, open reading frame (ORF)-first and concurrent models. It also examines how nascent loci acquire regulatory control and enter existing biological networks. The review then summarizes their evolutionary features, including weak ear
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent progress on de novo genes in plants, which arise from previously non-coding genomic regions and serve as a source of lineage-specific innovation. It covers the major models of gene birth (transcription-first, ORF-first, and concurrent), how nascent loci acquire regulatory control and integrate into biological networks, and their evolutionary features. The authors highlight the potential contributions of these genes to plant adaptation, trait diversity, and crop evolution.

papers.title: A Site-Aware Representation Learning Framework For Unified Molecular Interaction Modeling and Generative Design.
papers.abstract: Unifying drug-target affinity prediction and targeted molecular design within a single interpretable framework remains challenging. Many sequence-based affinity and design methods rely on global target representations without explicitly modeling binding regions, leading to site-level ambiguity in both screening and design. By contrast, structure-based methods require high-quality structural data and are poorly suited to dynamic targets. In this study, a new model named MolDBG is proposed as a unified site-aware framework that combines affinity prediction, binding-site identification, and affin
papers.summary: MolDBG is a unified site-aware framework that combines drug-target affinity prediction, binding-site identification, and targeted molecular design without requiring high-quality structural data. It addresses site-level ambiguity in sequence-based methods by explicitly modeling binding regions, making it suitable for dynamic targets.

papers.title: Gradient-based Optimization for mRNA Sequence Design.
papers.abstract: Designing mRNA coding sequences that simultaneously optimize RNA accessibility in the translation initiation region and codon adaptation while preserving the encoded protein requires navigating a vast discrete combinatorial space. The inherently discrete nature of codon choices prevents direct application of gradient-based optimization, despite the availability of accurate deep learning predictors such as DeepRaccess for RNA accessibility prediction.
papers.summary: This paper introduces a gradient-based optimization method for designing mRNA coding sequences that balances RNA accessibility in the translation initiation region with codon adaptation, while preserving the encoded protein. The approach overcomes the discrete nature of codon choices to leverage deep learning predictors like DeepRaccess, enabling more efficient exploration of the combinatorial sequence space.

papers.title: Engineered Transformer Base Editor with Enhanced Editing Efficiency.
papers.abstract: Canonical cytosine base editors (CBEs) achieve precise C-to-T conversions without inducing DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs), yet their clinical potential remains hampered by substantial off-target (OT) mutations. The recently developed transformer base editor (tBE) significantly reduces both genomic and transcriptomic OT mutations by using a cleavable deoxycytidine deaminase inhibitor (dCDI) domain. However, the modest base editing efficiency limits its broader applications. Here, through rational deaminase engineering and fusion of a uracil DNA glycosylase inhibitor (UGI) domain, we developed
papers.summary: The authors engineered an improved transformer base editor (tBE) by rationally modifying the deaminase and adding a uracil DNA glycosylase inhibitor (UGI) domain, aiming to boost editing efficiency while retaining the low off-target profile of the original tBE. This addresses a key limitation of the tBE system, whose modest base editing efficiency has restricted its broader use.

papers.title: Decoding gene regulation in plant genomes with artificial intelligence.
papers.abstract: One of the central goals of plant functional genomics is to uncover regulatory mechanisms that shape agriculturally important traits to inform crop improvement. Recent advances in machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI), especially Large Language Models (LLMs), have greatly transformed our ability to derive regulatory information from complex genomics data. This review starts with a brief introduction of recent advances in AI and ML. We then present a plant-focused synthesis of emerging applications of AI- and LLM tools to: (i) predict epigenomic features, regulatory DNA element
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent advances in applying machine learning and large language models to decode gene regulation in plant genomes, focusing on predicting epigenomic features and regulatory DNA elements. It highlights how AI tools can extract regulatory information from complex genomics data to inform crop improvement. The paper is aimed at plant functional genomics researchers seeking to leverage AI for understanding agriculturally important traits.

papers.title: Quantitative mapping from conventional MRI using self-supervised physics-guided deep learning: Applications to a large-scale, clinically heterogeneous dataset.
papers.abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a cornerstone of clinical neuroimaging, yet conventional MRIs provide qualitative information heavily dependent on scanner hardware and acquisition settings. While quantitative MRI (qMRI) offers intrinsic tissue parameters, the requirement for specialized acquisition protocols and reconstruction algorithms restricts its availability and impedes large-scale biomarker research. This study presents a self-supervised physics-guided deep learning framework to infer quantitative T1, T2, and proton-density (PD) maps directly from widely available clinical conventio
papers.summary: The authors present a self-supervised, physics-guided deep learning framework that infers quantitative MRI maps (T1, T2, proton density) directly from conventional clinical MRI scans, avoiding the need for specialized acquisition protocols. They demonstrate the approach on a large, clinically heterogeneous dataset, showing that quantitative tissue parameters can be recovered from routine imaging. This could enable large-scale retrospective biomarker research using existing clinical MRI archives.

papers.title: HyLnc: a hybrid deep learning and feature-based approach for long non-coding RNA prediction.
papers.abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play important roles in gene regulation, development and disease, yet accurate identification of lncRNAs from transcriptomic data remains a major computational challenge. Existing methods often rely either on handcrafted sequence features or deep learning approaches, each with inherent limitations in capturing the full complexity of RNA sequences. In this study, we proposed HyLnc, a computational framework that integrates transformer-based contextual embeddings with biologically meaningful sequence features for improved lncRNA prediction. A custom BERT-based mode
papers.summary: HyLnc is a computational framework that combines transformer-based contextual embeddings (a custom BERT model) with handcrafted biological sequence features to predict long non-coding RNAs from transcriptomic data. The hybrid approach aims to overcome the limitations of methods that rely solely on either handcrafted features or deep learning. This integration is intended to improve lncRNA identification accuracy.

papers.title: Deep generative models in biological sequence and structure analysis and design.
papers.abstract: Deep generative models have transformed biological sequence modeling from predictive analysis toward increasingly controllable design. Early biological applications of Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) established latent representation learning and sequence synthesis, while recent advances in transformer-based language models, discrete diffusion, flow-matching, and multimodal generative frameworks have substantially expanded the scope of biological design. This review examines generative models for DNA, RNA, and protein sequence design, emphasizing how
papers.summary: This review surveys deep generative models—from early VAEs and GANs to modern transformers, discrete diffusion, and flow-matching—applied to DNA, RNA, and protein sequence and structure design. It highlights the shift from predictive analysis toward controllable biological design and discusses multimodal frameworks that integrate sequence and structure information.

papers.title: A Novel Unsupervised Learning Model with Bayesian Hyperparameter Optimization for Predicting Substrates of Promiscuous Enzymes.
papers.abstract: Promiscuous enzymes catalyze multiple biochemical reactions, but predicting their substrate profiles remains challenging because annotations are incomplete, reliable negative labels are scarce, and enzyme-substrate relationships are inherently multilabel. Here, we present PreSEPM (Predictive Substrate Explorer for Promiscuous Enzymes), a sequence-only, closed-set framework that combines pretrained protein representations, Gaussian mixture modeling, cluster-substrate alignment, and Bayesian optimization of decision thresholds. PreSEPM operates within a predefined substrate panel and does not re
papers.summary: PreSEPM is a sequence-only, unsupervised machine learning framework that predicts which substrates a promiscuous enzyme can act on, using pretrained protein representations, Gaussian mixture modeling, and Bayesian optimization of decision thresholds. It addresses the scarcity of reliable negative labels and the multilabel nature of enzyme-substrate relationships by operating within a predefined substrate panel.

papers.title: Multimodal alignment improves generalizability of genomic biomarker prediction in computational pathology.
papers.abstract: Computational pathology models that use digitized histopathology whole-slide images have the potential to become a cost-effective and scalable alternative to molecular assays for the prediction of genomic biomarkers, a key task in precision oncology. However, as new genomic biomarkers are discovered or quantified, large, labeled datasets must be prospectively collected to train new models. To address this challenge, we developed multimodal alignment for biomarker learning and generalization (MARBLE), a multimodal contrastive pretraining strategy that integrates structured biomarker knowledge i
papers.summary: The paper introduces MARBLE, a multimodal contrastive pretraining strategy that aligns histopathology whole-slide images with structured genomic biomarker knowledge to improve generalization in computational pathology. This approach enables prediction of new or newly quantified genomic biomarkers without requiring large prospectively labeled datasets for each biomarker. The method demonstrates improved generalizability for biomarker prediction tasks in precision oncology.

papers.title: Humanizing Antibodies and Nanobodies From Scratch With HuDiff.
papers.abstract: Antibody (Ab) and nanobody (Nb) humanization is essential for reducing immunogenicity in therapeutic applications. HuDiff is an adaptive autoregressive diffusion approach that generates humanized antibodies and nanobodies from scratch using only complementarity-determining region sequences as input, eliminating the need for preexisting human templates. The method follows a two-stage training pipeline: pretraining on human antibody sequences to learn framework region patterns, followed by fine-tuning on target-species sequences. HuDiff-Ab processes paired heavy and light chains for conventional
papers.summary: HuDiff is a new adaptive autoregressive diffusion method that humanizes antibodies and nanobodies directly from complementarity-determining region sequences, without needing preexisting human templates. It uses a two-stage training pipeline—pretraining on human antibody sequences to learn framework patterns, then fine-tuning on target-species sequences—and handles paired heavy/light chains for conventional antibodies.

papers.title: Few-shot neuromorphic vision in a nonlinear photonic network laser.
papers.abstract: With the growing prevalence of artificial intelligence (AI), demand increases for hardware that mimics the brain's ability to extract structure from limited data. In the retina, ganglion cells detect features from sparse inputs via lateral inhibition, where neurons antagonistically suppress activity of neighboring cells. Biological neurons exhibit diverse heterogeneous nonlinear responses, linked to robust learning and strong performance in low-data regimes. Here, we introduce a retinally inspired photonic computing system where spatially competing lasing modes in a random network laser act as
papers.summary: This paper introduces a photonic computing system inspired by retinal lateral inhibition, using spatially competing lasing modes in a random network laser to perform neuromorphic vision tasks. The system leverages heterogeneous nonlinear responses to achieve few-shot learning, mimicking the brain's ability to extract structure from limited data.

papers.title: The fitness landscape of a form II rubisco in a photosynthetic bacterium guides engineering of oxygen tolerance.
papers.abstract: Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase (rubisco) is an important but challenging protein engineering target. Fast and selective rubiscos could enhance photosynthesis in plants and accelerate biobased production processes. To facilitate engineering of rubisco, we applied an in vivo screen that couples rubisco activity to growth rate of the photoautotrophic cyanobacterium Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803. We screened a barcoded mutagenesis library of the form II rubisco from Gallionella sp. containing 15,000 single-site and multi-site variants. Exchanges in loop 6 near the active site, at the
papers.summary: Researchers screened a barcoded library of 15,000 single- and multi-site variants of a form II rubisco from Gallionella sp. in the cyanobacterium Synechocystis, coupling rubisco activity to growth rate to map its fitness landscape. They identified key mutations, particularly in loop 6 near the active site, that influence catalytic activity and oxygen tolerance, providing a guide for engineering improved rubisco variants.

papers.title: Squidly harnesses enzyme functional hierarchy and contrastive learning to efficiently predict catalytic residues from sequence.
papers.abstract: Enzymes present a sustainable alternative to traditional chemical industries, drug synthesis, and bioremediation applications. Because catalytic residues are the key amino acids that drive enzyme function, their accurate prediction facilitates enzyme function prediction. Sequence similarity-based approaches such as BLAST are fast but require previously annotated homologues. Machine-learning (ML) approaches aim to overcome this limitation; however, current gold-standard ML-based methods require high-quality 3D structures limiting their application to large datasets. To address these challenges,
papers.summary: Squidly is a new machine-learning method that predicts which amino acids in an enzyme are catalytic directly from sequence, without needing 3D structures. It combines a hierarchical representation of enzyme function with contrastive learning, making it more scalable than structure-based gold-standard tools while outperforming simple homology searches.

papers.title: LLM-guided prediction of riboswitch-ligand binding affinity under data-limited conditions.
papers.abstract: Riboswitches are RNA regulatory elements that sense small molecules and regulate gene expression through ligand-induced conformational changes in an aptamer domain. They enable synthetic biology applications such as biosensing and gene circuit design. Accurate prediction of riboswitch-ligand binding affinity, quantified by the dissociation constant (Kd), is essential for rational riboswitch engineering. We present a neuro-symbolic framework in which LLM-derived embeddings encode riboswitch sequences, secondary structures, and ligand representations into a unified representation that captures r
papers.summary: The authors present a neuro-symbolic framework that uses LLM-derived embeddings to encode riboswitch sequences, secondary structures, and ligand representations for predicting riboswitch-ligand binding affinity (Kd). The approach is designed to work under data-limited conditions, where conventional machine learning models struggle due to scarce experimental binding data. This could support rational riboswitch engineering for synthetic biology applications like biosensing and gene circuits.

papers.title: Mapping the combinatorial coding between olfactory receptors and perception with deep learning.
papers.abstract: The sense of smell remains poorly understood compared with vision and audition. At its core is an information flow in which odorant molecules activate subsets of olfactory receptors (ORs) and combinations of receptor activations encode distinct percepts. However, predicting molecule-OR interactions, and linking them to perception, remains difficult. Here, we develop MolOR, an approach that maps odorants to their OR-activation profiles and then predicts their odor percepts. Using cross-attention between a graph neural network over molecules and protein-language-model embeddings of receptors, we
papers.summary: This paper introduces MolOR, a deep learning approach that predicts which olfactory receptors (ORs) are activated by a given odorant molecule and then uses those activation profiles to predict the resulting odor percept. It combines a graph neural network for molecules with protein language model embeddings for receptors via cross-attention, aiming to bridge the gap between chemical structure and smell perception.

papers.title: PMPIHGLL: predicting metabolite-protein interactions using dual hypergraph convolutional networks and large language models.
papers.abstract: Metabolite-protein interactions (MPIs) play pivotal roles in regulating cellular processes and metabolic pathways and have important implications for systems biology and drug discovery. Although several computational models have been proposed, alternative approaches are needed to broaden the methodological toolkit for MPI prediction. In this study, we developed a new deep-learning model for predicting MPIs. Chemical and protein large language models were used to generate informative representations of metabolites and proteins. For each entity type, we constructed two K-nearest-neighbor hypergr
papers.summary: This paper introduces PMPIHGLL, a deep-learning model that predicts interactions between metabolites and proteins by combining chemical and protein large language model embeddings with dual hypergraph convolutional networks. The approach captures higher-order relationships among metabolites and proteins, aiming to broaden the computational toolkit for MPI prediction relevant to systems biology and drug discovery.

papers.title: KGTC-DDA:Drug-disease association prediction based on parallel graph isomorphism and transformer networks with cross-attention.
papers.abstract: Drug development is a complex, time-consuming, and costly process, making drug repurposing an important strategy for identifying new therapeutic applications for existing drugs. Computational drug-disease association (DDA) prediction has therefore attracted increasing attention in recent years. Although many existing methods incorporate similarity information and graph neural networks for DDA prediction, effectively capturing both local structural patterns and global dependencies, as well as modeling complex interactions between drugs and diseases, remains challenging. To address these limitat
papers.summary: KGTC-DDA is a computational framework that predicts drug-disease associations by combining parallel graph isomorphism networks with transformer networks and cross-attention mechanisms. The approach aims to capture both local structural patterns and global dependencies in drug-disease knowledge graphs, improving drug repurposing predictions over existing similarity- and GNN-based methods.

papers.title: DLRNA-BERTa: a transformer approach for predicting molecule-RNA binding affinities.
papers.abstract: Therapies targeting RNA are rapidly expanding, with 24 FDA-approved RNA therapeutics and over 130 currently in clinical trials, highlighting RNA's growing role in drug discovery. In this context, transformer-based language models provide a scalable and cost-effective approach to accelerate RNA-targeted drug discovery by enabling the prediction of molecule-RNA binding affinities directly from sequence information. This study introduces DLRNA-BERTa, a RoBERTa-based framework that integrates RNA-BERTa and ChemBERTa-v2 to model molecule-RNA binding affinities. The framework includes six RNA class-
papers.summary: DLRNA-BERTa is a transformer-based framework that combines RNA-BERTa and ChemBERTa-v2 to predict binding affinities between small molecules and RNA directly from sequence information. This approach aims to accelerate RNA-targeted drug discovery by providing a scalable, cost-effective alternative to experimental binding assays.

papers.title: ELISA (Embedding-Linked Interactive Single-cell Agent): an interpretable hybrid generative Artificial Intelligence agent for expression-grounded discovery in single-cell genomics.
papers.abstract: Translating single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data into mechanistic biological hypotheses remains a critical bottleneck, as agentic AI systems lack direct access to transcriptomic representations while expression foundation models remain opaque to natural language. Here, we introduce ELISA (Embedding-Linked Interactive Single-cell Agent), an interpretable framework that unifies single-cell generative pretrained transformer expression embeddings with biomedical bidirectional encoder representations from transformers-based semantic retrieval and large-language model (LLM)-mediated interpret
papers.summary: ELISA is a hybrid AI agent that combines single-cell expression embeddings (from a generative pretrained transformer) with biomedical text retrieval and LLM-based interpretation to help researchers generate mechanistic hypotheses from scRNA-seq data. It bridges the gap between opaque expression foundation models and natural-language reasoning, aiming to make single-cell analysis more interpretable and discovery-oriented.

papers.title: LAMBDA: a prophage detection benchmark for genomic language models.
papers.abstract: Transformer-based genomic sequence models represent an emerging frontier in computational biology. Yet, their embeddings have not yet shown the same level of predictive power as natural and protein language models, highlighting a gap between current implementations and theoretical promise. Existing benchmarks for DNA language models primarily focus on classifying regulatory elements in eukaryotic genomes, leaving open the fundamental question of whether these models learn sequence-level features across whole genomes. We introduce LAMBDA, a benchmark designed to rigorously evaluate genome langu
papers.summary: LAMBDA is a new benchmark for evaluating genomic language models on prophage detection, a task that requires learning sequence-level features across whole genomes rather than just regulatory elements. The authors use it to test whether transformer-based DNA models capture meaningful genomic signals, addressing a gap in existing benchmarks that focus mainly on eukaryotic regulatory classification.

papers.title: CAREPath: semantic context-aware reasoning paths with mechanism-augmented embeddings for drug repurposing.
papers.abstract: Biomedical knowledge graphs that include drugs, genes, and diseases support drug repurposing by connecting drugs to diseases through gene-mediated multi-hop paths, thereby enabling mechanism-of-action reasoning. However, deeper traversal does not necessarily improve mechanistic reasoning: long paths grow combinatorially and frequently pass through hub genes, producing irrelevant gene regulatory signals, whereas overly constrained or sparse paths may miss broader biological context. We propose Context-Aware REasoning Path (CAREPath), a knowledge graph (KG)-large language model framework inspire
papers.summary: CAREPath is a knowledge graph–LLM framework for drug repurposing that generates semantic context-aware reasoning paths connecting drugs to diseases via genes, addressing the problem that longer paths in biomedical KGs often traverse hub genes and introduce irrelevant regulatory signals. It uses mechanism-augmented embeddings to balance path depth and biological relevance, aiming to improve mechanism-of-action reasoning for identifying new drug indications.

papers.title: DNAmBERT: a transformer-based model for non-invasive cancer diagnosis using DNA sequence and methylation data.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation alterations are early and stable hallmarks of cancer and represent promising biomarkers for non-invasive detection using circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA). However, current computational approaches often model DNA sequence and methylation features separately and struggle to capture complex read-level methylation architecture in heterogeneous, low-signal liquid biopsy data. Here, we present DNAmBERT, a Transformer-based deep learning framework designed to jointly model DNA sequence context and read-level methylation haplotype structure from cfDNA methylation sequencing data. DNA
papers.summary: DNAmBERT is a Transformer-based deep learning framework that jointly models DNA sequence context and read-level methylation haplotype structure from circulating cell-free DNA to enable non-invasive cancer detection. Unlike prior methods that treat sequence and methylation features separately, it captures complex read-level methylation architecture in low-signal liquid biopsy data.

papers.title: AResKGLM: a graph-grounded language-model framework for interpretable multi-hop antimicrobial resistance reasoning.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) threatens microbiology and microbiome bioinformatics because resistance phenotypes are shaped by interactions among genes, mobile genetic elements, and functional environments across microbial communities. Prioritizing resistance determinants requires models that reason across knowledge graphs (KGs) linking genes, proteins, pathways, drugs, and microbial phenotypes. Existing graph-based methods compress this evidence into scalar scores, whereas large language models can produce explanations not grounded in structured evidence. We developed AResKGLM (Antimicrobial
papers.summary: AResKGLM is a framework that combines knowledge graphs linking AMR-related genes, proteins, pathways, drugs, and microbial phenotypes with large language models to enable interpretable multi-hop reasoning about antimicrobial resistance. It addresses the limitation of existing graph methods that collapse evidence into scalar scores and of LLMs that generate explanations ungrounded in structured evidence. The approach aims to prioritize resistance determinants while producing explanations traceable to structured knowledge.

papers.title: From rules to foundation models: a comprehensive review of machine learning approaches for siRNA design.
papers.abstract: Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) are a clinically validated therapeutic modality with eight FDA-approved drugs, yet designing effective siRNAs remains computationally challenging due to complex dependencies on sequence composition, thermodynamic properties, target-site accessibility, and off-target interactions. Over two decades, computational approaches have evolved from empirical heuristics to deep learning systems integrating physical priors with learned representations. We review the complete landscape of machine learning methods for siRNA design, spanning classical scoring rules, pretraine
papers.summary: This review surveys the evolution of computational methods for designing small interfering RNAs (siRNAs), from early empirical rules to modern deep learning and foundation models. It highlights how these approaches integrate sequence, thermodynamic, and structural features to improve siRNA efficacy and specificity, covering the full landscape of machine learning techniques.

papers.title: An O-glycosylation-based prognostic signature for biochemical recurrence in prostate cancer identifies GALNTL6 as a potential promoter of malignant phenotypes.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is frequently diagnosed in men, and biochemical recurrence (BCR) remains a persistent problem after clinical treatment. Commonly used indicators do not identify patients who are likely to relapse early. Protein O-linked glycosylation is an important post-translational modification involved in cancer progression, but its prognostic relevance and regulatory mechanisms in PCa remain insufficiently understood. GALNTL6, which encodes polypeptide N-acetylgalactosaminyltransferase-like 6, is putatively involved in mucin-type protein O-linked glycosylation and remains poorly char
papers.summary: This study developed a prognostic signature based on O-glycosylation-related genes to predict biochemical recurrence in prostate cancer patients, addressing a gap where current clinical indicators fail to identify early relapse risk. The authors identified GALNTL6 as a potential driver of malignant phenotypes, suggesting it may promote aggressive disease through altered protein O-linked glycosylation. The work highlights O-glycosylation as a promising avenue for improving prostate cancer prognosis and understanding its progression mechanisms.

papers.title: Integrated transcriptome analysis and machine learning to construct a homeostatic model of acetylation for bladder cancer and validate the key gene CES1.
papers.abstract: Bladder cancer (BLCA) is one of the most common malignant tumors of the urinary system. Protein acetylation (PA) plays a critical role in regulating multiple biological processes (BPs), cellular homeostasis, and cancer-related signaling pathways. This study aimed to construct a homeostatic model of acetylation for BLCA using integrated transcriptome analysis and machine learning and to validate the key gene CES1.
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptome data with machine learning to build a homeostatic model of protein acetylation for bladder cancer, aiming to identify acetylation-related genes with prognostic or functional relevance. The authors validate CES1 as a key gene within this model, suggesting it plays a role in bladder cancer biology. The work is a computational modeling effort with limited experimental validation.

papers.title: CCNA2 orchestrates the PI3K/AKT signaling axis to propel prostate cancer metastasis.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) remains one of the most common malignancies in men, posing a persistent global burden in terms of both public health and socioeconomic costs. Although early detection is essential for improving patient outcomes, existing clinical tools, including prostate-specific antigen (PSA) screening, digital rectal examination, and transrectal ultrasound-guided biopsy, are hampered by suboptimal specificity and positive predictive value, resulting in frequent overdiagnosis and overtreatment of indolent lesions while missing a subset of aggressive tumors at an early stage. In this con
papers.summary: This study identifies CCNA2 (cyclin A2) as a driver of prostate cancer metastasis through activation of the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. The findings suggest CCNA2 could serve as a potential biomarker or therapeutic target for aggressive prostate cancer, addressing limitations of current PSA-based screening.

papers.title: Machine learning-based prediction and external validation of treatment-related myelosuppression in patients with non-small cell lung cancer receiving PD-1 inhibitors plus platinum-doublet chemotherapy.
papers.abstract: The application of programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) inhibitors combined with platinum-based double-drug chemotherapy in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is becoming increasingly widespread. However, the impact of this treatment regimen on the bone marrow hematopoietic system is well-defined. Therefore, we have to consider the risk of bone marrow suppression in NSCLC patients after receiving this treatment regimen. Our objective was to identify risk factors for the risk of myelosuppression, one of the serious complications of PD-1 inhibitor plus platinum-based dual-agent c
papers.summary: This study developed and externally validated machine learning models to predict treatment-related myelosuppression in NSCLC patients receiving PD-1 inhibitors plus platinum-doublet chemotherapy. The authors identified risk factors associated with bone marrow suppression and assessed model performance on an independent cohort. The work aims to support early risk stratification for this increasingly common treatment regimen.

papers.title: Investigating the mechanisms of PhIP-induced colorectal cancer through network toxicology, machine learning, and molecular dynamics simulation.
papers.abstract: Over the past few years, 2-amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo[4,5-b]pyridine (PhIP)- a compound from grilled or processed meats-has emerged as a major player in cancer development, especially colorectal cancer (CRC). This work dives into its potential links to CRC and uncovers the key genes that bridge this connection.
papers.summary: This study uses network toxicology, machine learning, and molecular dynamics simulations to identify key genes linking the dietary carcinogen PhIP (found in grilled and processed meats) to colorectal cancer. The work aims to uncover molecular mechanisms underlying PhIP-induced CRC, potentially highlighting targets for further investigation.

papers.title: Development and internal validation of an interpretable machine learning prognostic prediction model for postoperative delirium after esophagectomy.
papers.abstract: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a frequent neurological complication associated with adverse outcomes after esophagectomy. Existing risk-assessment tools may provide limited individualized prognostic information. This study aimed to develop and internally validate an interpretable machine learning (ML) prognostic prediction model for POD after esophagectomy.
papers.summary: This study developed and internally validated an interpretable machine learning model to predict postoperative delirium in patients undergoing esophagectomy, a common and serious neurological complication. The model aims to provide more individualized prognostic information than existing risk-assessment tools, with interpretability features to support clinical decision-making.

papers.title: A token-pruning framework enables efficient representation of the human genome for RNA modification analysis.
papers.abstract: Modelling long genomic sequences remains challenging due to extreme sequence length, high redundancy, and the need for biological interpretability. Although Transformer-based architectures have achieved strong performance across genomic tasks, their high computational cost and reliance on fixed tokenization strategies limit their scalability and ability to focus on biologically informative regions.
papers.summary: The authors propose a token-pruning framework that reduces the computational burden of Transformer models on long genomic sequences by discarding uninformative tokens, enabling efficient representation of the human genome for RNA modification analysis. This approach addresses the scalability limits of fixed tokenization strategies while preserving biologically informative regions.

papers.title: Rational and computation-assisted engineering of a compact and efficient CRISPR-Cas12f genome editor.
papers.abstract: The CRISPR-Cas12f system is an ultracompact genome-editing platform, yet only a few orthologs exhibit robust activity in mammalian cells. Here, we systematically screened 23 Cas12f orthologs and identified two active nucleases, PspCas12f1 and TcCas12f1, capable of genome editing in human cells. sgRNA scaffold optimization enhanced the basal activity of PspCas12f1. To further improve its performance, we combined structure-guided rational design with protein language model-assisted filtering. Candidate mutations predicted by SaProt were further screened based on structural proximity to the DNA-b
papers.journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy
papers.summary: The authors systematically screened 23 Cas12f orthologs and identified two active nucleases, PspCas12f1 and TcCas12f1, that can edit human genomes. By optimizing the sgRNA scaffold and combining structure-guided rational design with a protein language model (SaProt) to filter mutations near the DNA-binding interface, they engineered a compact and more efficient Cas12f genome editor.

papers.title: Plasma Metabolites for Identifying Bacterial Infection in Acute-on-chronic Liver Failure: A Prospective Multicenter Study.
papers.abstract: Bacterial infection is a key cause of mortality in patients with acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF). In this study, we aimed to identify metabolite biomarkers and develop a novel machine learning model for early identification of bacterial infection in ACLF.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical and translational hepatology
papers.summary: This prospective multicenter study aimed to identify plasma metabolite biomarkers and develop a machine learning model for early detection of bacterial infection in patients with acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF), a condition where infection is a major cause of death. The work demonstrates the potential of metabolomics combined with machine learning to improve early diagnosis in this high-risk patient population.

papers.title: Integrative Multi-omics and Machine Learning Reveal the Therapeutic Mechanisms of Juanyu-Xiaozhi Formula in Metabolic Dysfunction-associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Hepatic Fibrosis via the AP-1/PPARγ/SCD1 Axis.
papers.abstract: Despite the surging global prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and related liver fibrosis, effective treatments remain limited. While the traditional Chinese medicine Juanyu-Xiaozhi Formula (JYXZF) is used against MASLD, its bioactive components and mechanisms are poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects of JYXZF and elucidate its underlying mechanisms of action.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical and translational hepatology
papers.summary: This study combines multi-omics profiling with machine learning to investigate how the traditional Chinese medicine formula Juanyu-Xiaozhi (JYXZF) treats metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and liver fibrosis. The authors identify the AP-1/PPARγ/SCD1 axis as a key mechanistic pathway underlying the formula's therapeutic effects. The work provides a framework for understanding the bioactive components and molecular targets of a complex herbal formula in liver disease.

papers.title: Dynamics-aware geometric learning predicts disease-associated molecular perturbations.
papers.abstract: Missense mutations and post-translational modifications (PTMs) are major molecular perturbations that reshape protein function but are traditionally studied independently. Current computational approaches largely rely on sequence conservation or static structural features, limiting our understanding of how perturbations alter intrinsic protein dynamics. We present DynGeo-Pheno, a unified geometric deep learning framework that integrates protein language model representations with anisotropic network model-derived dynamics to jointly capture evolutionary, structural, and biophysical information
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: DynGeo-Pheno is a geometric deep learning framework that combines protein language model embeddings with anisotropic network model-derived dynamics to predict the effects of missense mutations and post-translational modifications on protein function. By incorporating intrinsic protein dynamics rather than relying only on sequence conservation or static structures, it offers a unified approach to studying these two major classes of molecular perturbations.

papers.title: ITGBL1 and RPN1 Mark a Fibrotic NP Subpopulation with Coupled Integrin Signaling and N-Glycosylation Programs in IVDD.
papers.abstract: FibroNPC is a degeneration associated subtype in intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), yet its markers and immune crosstalk remain poorly characterized. ITGBL1 and RPN1 recur as IVDD associated genes in bulk studies, but where they are expressed within the heterogeneous disc has not been resolved.
papers.summary: This study identifies ITGBL1 and RPN1 as markers of a fibrotic nucleus pulposus cell subpopulation (FibroNPC) associated with intervertebral disc degeneration, linking integrin signaling and N-glycosylation programs. It resolves where these previously bulk-level IVDD-associated genes are expressed within the heterogeneous disc and explores their immune crosstalk.

papers.title: Multimodal molecular features enable interpretable umami peptide screening and structure-activity analysis.
papers.abstract: Umami peptides are important taste-active components in protein-rich foods, but their computational discovery is still constrained by predictors that rely mainly on sequence information and provide limited mechanistic interpretability. In this study, BioPP-GFD was developed as an interpretable multimodal deep learning framework for umami peptide screening and structure-activity analysis. The model integrates molecular graphs, molecular fingerprints, and physicochemical descriptors through adaptive channel attention. In the umami-bitter peptide classification task, BioPP-GFD achieved an accurac
papers.summary: The authors developed BioPP-GFD, an interpretable multimodal deep learning framework that combines molecular graphs, fingerprints, and physicochemical descriptors to screen for umami peptides and analyze their structure-activity relationships. The model outperformed sequence-only predictors in distinguishing umami from bitter peptides, offering mechanistic interpretability through adaptive channel attention.

papers.title: Integrating machine learning and GWAS for variant prioritization in the INCIPE cohort highlights ABC transporter genes in chronic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major public health challenge, affecting approximately 674 million people worldwide and representing one of the fastest-growing causes of mortality. Since CKD is frequently asymptomatic in its early stages, the identification of novel genetic biomarkers may improve early detection and risk stratification. Genome-Wide Association Studies (GWAS) have identified numerous genetic loci associated with CKD and related traits; however, their performance is often limited in small and imbalanced cohorts, where reduced statistical power increases both false-positive and
papers.summary: This study integrates machine learning with GWAS to prioritize genetic variants in the INCIPE cohort, addressing the limited statistical power of traditional GWAS in small, imbalanced cohorts. The approach highlights ABC transporter genes as potentially relevant to chronic kidney disease risk. The work demonstrates how ML can complement GWAS for biomarker discovery in underpowered study settings.

papers.title: Integrating single-cell transcriptomics to construct an oncogene-driven prognostic model and elucidate metabolic-immune crosstalk in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related deaths, its progression and treatment heterogeneity are mainly influenced by driver gene and tumor micro-environment (TME) interactions. Nevertheless, the mechanisms of this process at the single-cell level remain unclear. This study integrated TCGA and multi-center single-cell transcriptome data to identify a 575 genes HCC-specific core set, developing a single-cell "oncogene scoring" system to quantify individual carcinogenic activity. This score is significantly elevated in malignant and proliferative T cells and is closely
papers.summary: This study integrates TCGA bulk transcriptomics with multi-center single-cell transcriptome data to define a 575-gene HCC-specific core set and build a single-cell 'oncogene scoring' system that quantifies carcinogenic activity per cell. The score is elevated in malignant and proliferative T cells and is linked to metabolic-immune crosstalk, supporting a prognostic model for hepatocellular carcinoma.

papers.title: BeitAI-pHLA: Multiallele Peptide-HLA Class I Binding Prediction Using Protein Language Model and Multi-Instance Learning.
papers.abstract: Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules participate in cellular immune responses by binding to peptide fragments derived from antigens. Exploring this process is crucial to understanding the mechanisms and underlying factors that regulate the cellular immune system. Due to the extreme polymorphism of HLA, the peptides obtained from mass spectrometry of eluted ligand experiments typically correspond to multiple HLA alleles. They are thus poly-specific, providing various options for HLA assignments. This introduces notable challenges for accurate peptide-HLA assignment and interpretation. To add
papers.summary: BeitAI-pHLA is a computational tool that predicts which peptide fragments will bind to class I HLA molecules, a key step in cellular immune recognition. It uses a protein language model combined with multi-instance learning to handle the challenge that mass-spectrometry eluted ligands often come from multiple HLA alleles at once, making binding assignment ambiguous. This approach aims to improve accurate peptide-HLA assignment and interpretation across highly polymorphic HLA types.

papers.title: Development and validation of machine learning models for 30-day mortality prediction in septic shock.
papers.abstract: Septic shock carries a high risk of death, yet traditional prognostic tools have limitations. This study aimed to develop and validate machine learning (ML) models for predicting 30-day mortality in septic shock patients using comprehensive admission variables.
papers.summary: This study develops and validates machine learning models to predict 30-day mortality in patients with septic shock using comprehensive admission variables. The work aims to overcome limitations of traditional prognostic tools by leveraging ML approaches for improved risk stratification.

papers.title: DBP-CanPred: a machine learning model for predicting cancer-causing mutations in DNA-binding proteins.
papers.abstract: The fundamental cellular processes, including transcriptional regulation, chromatin organization, and genome maintenance, are regulated by DNA-binding proteins (DBPs). Mutations in DBPs can alter protein-DNA interactions, leading to tumor development. However, identifying such driver mutations remains a major challenge due to limitations of experimental approaches.
papers.summary: DBP-CanPred is a machine learning model designed to predict cancer-causing mutations specifically in DNA-binding proteins. It addresses the challenge of identifying driver mutations that disrupt protein-DNA interactions, which are difficult to detect experimentally. The tool aims to aid in prioritizing mutations for further study in cancer genomics.

papers.title: Study of deep learning cues for cross linguistic part of speech tagging in English- Malayalam code-mixed data.
papers.abstract: Part Of Speech (POS) tagging is a fundamental task in Natural Language Processing (NLP) that assigns grammatical labels to words in a sentence. Code mixed text, which entails switching between two or more languages within a single conversation or a sentence, presents challenges for POS tagging. This investigation entailed a comprehensive study of deep learning approaches for cross linguistic POS tagging, focused on English Malayalam code mixed data prevalent on social media platforms. The study was carried out on linguistically complex and varied English Malayalam code mixed text from social m
papers.summary: This study evaluates deep learning approaches for part-of-speech tagging in English-Malayalam code-mixed social media text, a linguistically challenging setting where two languages are mixed within a single sentence. The authors systematically compare different neural architectures and embedding strategies to identify which cues best support cross-linguistic POS tagging in this low-resource, code-mixed context.

papers.title: Predicting food taste with bound-driven optimization.
papers.abstract: The prediction of sensory attributes from ingredient-level formulations is an emerging challenge at the intersection of food science and artificial intelligence. We address the fundamental question of whether the taste of a food can be predicted from its ingredients by treating recipes as composite materials. We apply Hashin-Shtrikman (HS) and Reuss-Voigt (RV) bounds, techniques originally developed for elastic moduli, as a null-hypothesis additive baseline for five taste dimensions (sweetness, sourness, bitterness, umami, saltiness) on a curated dataset of 70 recipes decomposed into 115 disti
papers.summary: This study tests whether the taste of a food can be predicted from its ingredient composition by borrowing bounds techniques (Hashin-Shtrikman and Reuss-Voigt) originally developed for materials science. Using a curated dataset of 70 recipes decomposed into 115 distinct ingredients, the authors establish an additive baseline for five taste dimensions: sweetness, sourness, bitterness, umami, and saltiness. The work frames recipe formulation as a composite-materials problem, offering a null-hypothesis benchmark for future taste-prediction models.

papers.title: Discovery and validation of a multi-protein panel for predicting non-fatal major adverse cardiovascular events in diabetic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: To identify plasma protein biomarkers associated with incident non-fatal major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in diabetic kidney disease (DKD) patients.
papers.summary: This study aimed to identify plasma protein biomarkers that predict non-fatal major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with diabetic kidney disease. By analyzing plasma proteins, the authors discovered and validated a multi-protein panel associated with incident MACE, which could improve cardiovascular risk stratification in this high-risk population.

papers.title: Extreme phenotype-derived machine learning reveals susceptibility and resilience signatures for severe diabetic retinopathy.
papers.abstract: The mechanisms underlying why some individuals with diabetes develop severe diabetic retinopathy (DR), whereas others remain free of retinal complications despite long-standing disease, remain incompletely understood. We aimed to identify systemic susceptibility and resilience signatures associated with severe DR using an extreme phenotype-derived machine learning framework.
papers.summary: This study uses an extreme phenotype machine learning approach to identify systemic signatures that distinguish diabetes patients who develop severe diabetic retinopathy from those who remain resistant despite long-standing disease. The framework aims to uncover molecular or clinical markers of susceptibility versus resilience to severe DR.

papers.title: Skill-File-Guided Virtual Screening: A Single-Target Formyl Peptide Receptor 2 Case Study of Large-Language-Model-Coordinated Physics and Diffusion Docking.
papers.abstract: Background: Virtual screening outcomes depend on protocol choices normally made implicitly by experts. I tested whether encoding that expertise as a "skill file" (a Markdown reference read by a large-language-model coding agent) changes virtual screening outcomes versus naive agent defaults, in a single-target case study on formyl peptide receptor 2 (FPR2; Protein Data Bank 7T6S, 3.0 Å cryo-electron microscopy). Methods: A Claude Code agent curated 1,000 pChEMBL ≥5 FPR2 actives and 9,829 property-matched decoys, prepared ligand libraries under naive and skill-guided protocols, and screened the
papers.summary: This case study tests whether giving a large-language-model coding agent a curated 'skill file' of expert virtual screening protocols improves docking-based hit identification against formyl peptide receptor 2 (FPR2), compared to naive agent defaults. The agent assembled 1,000 known FPR2 actives and 9,829 property-matched decoys and ran physics-based and diffusion docking under both protocols. The work illustrates how encoding expert heuristics into LLM agent workflows can systematically change virtual screening outcomes.

papers.title: Integrating domain-specific convolutional features with Swin Transformers for transparent cervical cancer diagnostics.
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer screening relies heavily on manual cytopathological evaluation, which is subjective and prone to inter-observer variability. While deep learning offers automated alternatives, existing models often struggle to capture both global cellular context and fine-grained biological nuances. To address this, we propose CAMF-Swin, a novel hybrid architecture for precise cervical cell classification.
papers.summary: The authors propose CAMF-Swin, a hybrid deep learning architecture that combines domain-specific convolutional features with Swin Transformers to classify cervical cells for cancer screening. The approach aims to capture both global cellular context and fine-grained biological detail, addressing limitations of existing automated cytopathology models. The work targets improved accuracy and transparency in cervical cancer diagnostics.

papers.title: Interpretable prediction of nucleic acid-binding proteins using a protein language model.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of DNA-binding proteins (DBPs) and RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) is critical for elucidating transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulatory mechanisms. However, existing computational approaches often rely on inferred labels or domain-specific annotations, which limit the subsequent generalizability.
papers.summary: This paper presents an interpretable method for predicting DNA- and RNA-binding proteins using a protein language model, aiming to overcome the limitations of existing approaches that depend on inferred labels or domain-specific annotations. The approach is designed to improve generalizability in identifying nucleic acid-binding proteins, which are key to transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulation.

papers.title: DeepVIC: modular prediction and classification of bacterial virulence factors using protein language model embeddings.
papers.abstract: Virulence factors (VFs) play critical roles in bacterial pathogenesis, and identifying these proteins and elucidating their mechanisms is essential for developing effective infection treatments. While protein language models (PLMs) have revolutionized the protein analysis, current in silico methods for classifying VFs primarily rely on fine-tuned PLMs ProtBert-BFD that perform identification and classification in a single step. This monolithic approach lacks flexibility and is vulnerable to error propagation, particularly from false negatives. Moreover, the direct use of PLM embeddings as feat
papers.summary: DeepVIC introduces a modular framework for predicting and classifying bacterial virulence factors by leveraging protein language model embeddings, separating the identification and classification steps rather than using a monolithic fine-tuned model. This design reduces error propagation, particularly from false negatives, and improves flexibility compared to prior single-step approaches like ProtBert-BFD.

papers.title: Computational mapping of resistance-relevant signals in proteins using deep and classical feature spaces.
papers.abstract: The functional diversity of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) proteins necessitates advanced computational frameworks capable of capturing complex macromolecular signatures beyond simple sequence homology. While traditional alignment-based tools identify known resistance determinants, they often overlook the underlying biochemical and structural properties that define novel or divergent resistant macromolecules.
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational framework that combines deep learning and classical feature representations to map resistance-relevant signals in antimicrobial resistance (AMR) proteins. By moving beyond sequence homology, it aims to capture biochemical and structural properties that could reveal novel or divergent resistance determinants. The approach highlights the potential of feature-space mapping for improving AMR protein identification and characterization.

papers.title: SA-FGPN: Stability-aware feature-gated progressive learning for pediatric brain tumor classification from high dimensional gene expression data.
papers.abstract: Accurate pediatric brain tumor classification from gene expression data remains challenging due to the extremely high-dimensional nature of transcriptomic datasets, where tens of thousands of features are available from only a limited number of samples. This imbalance increases the risk of overfitting, unstable feature selection, and unreliable performance estimation. Moreover, molecular heterogeneity among pediatric brain tumor subtypes makes robust prediction and biological interpretation difficult. This study aims to develop a stable and interpretable deep learning framework for pediatric b
papers.summary: The authors present SA-FGPN, a deep learning framework designed to classify pediatric brain tumor subtypes from high-dimensional gene expression data. The method addresses the common problem of overfitting and unstable feature selection when there are far more features than samples by using stability-aware feature gating and progressive learning. This aims to improve both prediction robustness and biological interpretability in a challenging clinical setting.
